QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_2

question.text: Before the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012 came into force, how did offshore hedge funds typically gain Indian market exposure for their foreign investors, as discussed in the chapter?

answer.text: By investing through FII registrations or via Offshore Derivative Instruments (ODIs) issued by FIIs against underlying Indian securities
By setting up domiciled hedge funds in India under the SEBI (Mutual Fund) Regulations
By registering as Category III AIFs directly with SEBI
By registering as Portfolio Managers under the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter states foreign investors deployed capital via hedge funds and funds-of-funds set up in offshore jurisdictions, investing directly in Indian securities or through ODIs issued by FIIs. SEBI gave hedge funds a limited window up to 2012 to register under the FII Regulations with additional safeguards before the AIF framework was formalised. The Trap: Option C is anachronistic — Cat III AIF only existed after 2012. Option B is false; no hedge funds were domiciled in India pre-2012. Option D confuses PMS (separate managed accounts) with pooled hedge vehicles. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/XIX-D cover the Cat I/II evolution (VC/PE roots). XIX-E and XIX-B cover the hedge-fund branch of the story — pre-2012 offshore structure, ODIs via FIIs, and the 2012 formalisation as Cat III. Manager's Pro-Tip: When your FPI investor onboards today, you still see the legacy ODI plumbing in prime-broker agreements. Cat III AIFs now regulate what used to be offshore-only. Check FEMA Notification 355/2015 for the current NRI/FPI investment routing into Cat III.
